routing_result.work: Shop owners lose fewer sales to abandoned carts — more of the carts customers leave behind end up as finished orders (seeing which carts are abandoned today, and reminding customers to come back and finish)

placements.why: The goal is about the shopper's Acquire intent (cart -> checkout) breaking off; the ecommerce shelf is the only one whose trigger names cart and orders, and its Acquire intelligence line is the only shelf line about cart abandonment. Medium, not high: the shelf names it as an intelligence feature, not as a capability with functionalities, so abandoned-cart recovery has no capability of its own on the shelf.
conditions: core intelligence tier — 'should be on the table early, not bolted on' (no profile key named)

placements.why: Telling a cart that ended without an order apart from one that became an order rests on the cart and order records this capability keeps; it is the record underneath the goal, not the goal itself.
conditions: Level 1 — the floor, every store that sells

placements.why: A reminder to a customer who has left the shop is an away-from-app, lifecycle message — the notifications trigger; the domain owns how it reaches the customer, while the reason to send it stays in ecommerce.
conditions: Email — when shape.surfaces includes web/api and you need durable, away-from-app reach

placements.why: A one-click reminder to a shopper is only sendable with consent and must not turn into spam; the shelf makes consent and frequency discipline non-negotiable for any send.
conditions: Opt-in / opt-out — nfr.privacy >= medium, or compliance includes GDPR
Fatigue / frequency control — when volume rises, or shape.stage is public/monetized
